title: Strong Ulam Stability Characterizes Amenability
main_claim: A countable discrete group is strongly Ulam stable (uniform stability of unitary almost-representations on arbitrary Hilbert spaces) iff it is amenable; the new direction constructs, for nonamenable G and every δ>0, a map μ:G→U(H) with def(μ)<δ at uniform distance >1/10 from every representation.

issues.description: Absolute constants C (from the priority lemma, the truncation lemma and the frame orthonormalization) are never made explicit, and C may change between occurrences. The parameter order L→η→β handles this correctly, because every N-dependent term is multiplied by η and η is chosen after N. So this is a presentational looseness, not a gap.
issues.evidence: Defect bound Ch+CNη+CNhη; L is chosen first so that Ch<δ/2, then η, then β<min(β0(η),1/(3200N)). I checked that this order closes: 2√(2Nβ)<1/20 and 1/10+1/20+1/20=1/5<1/4.
